item.title: LAUTECH ASUU begins indefinite strike
item.description: By Adeola Badru Academic activities have been disrupted at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH), Ogbomoso, Oyo State, following the commencement of an indefinite strike by the institution’s chapter of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) on Thursday. The industrial action followed the expiration of a 14-day ultimatum issued by the union to the university management over outstanding demands, including the implementation of the 2025 Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN)-ASUU Agreement and the payment of consequential arrears dating back to January 2026. The union is also demanding the immediate payment of outstanding Earned Academic Allowances (EAA) and promotion arrears covering the period from 2013 to 2025. According to ASUU, the university’s Governing Council formally accepted and approved the implementation of the December 2025 FGN-ASUU Agreement. However, the union said the management had repeatedly cited a lack of funds as the reason for delays in implementation. Beyond the financial demands, the union is seeking the resolution of several administrative and governance issues before the Vice-Chancellor and the university management. These include concerns about the composition of the Staff Disciplinary Committee, the reconstitution of the Committee of Provosts and Deans, and transparency in the university’s electronic voting system. In a statement jointly signed by the branch Chairperson, Prof. Olujimi Dada, and the Secretary, Dr Soji Arinola, the union expressed frustration over the failure to resolve the issues despite repeated attempts at formal and informal dialogue. The union said it decided to embark on the indefinite strike after exhausting several avenues of engagement without reaching a resolution. It urged members to remain united throughout the industrial action and advised them to disregard information or directives not issued directly by the branch chairperson. The union stressed that only information and directives issued by the branch chairperson should be treated as authentic during the strike. The post LAUTECH ASUU begins indefinite strike appeared first on Vanguard News .

Currently with Dana White’s Zuffa Boxing, professional boxer Edgar Berlanga has been arrested . The 29-year-old is currently facing charges following an alleged domestic dispute with the mother of his child. The incident resulted in his arrest on Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, in Polk County, Florida. The charges of domestic violence aggravated battery and domestic battery against him arise from an alleged event on Oct. 18, 2026. The mentioned felony charge can result in a prison term of up to 15 years. As per the police report filed by Lakeland Police Department and court documents obtained by TMZ, Berlanga and his baby’s mother were driving when they got into an argument, shortly after visiting a gun range. The woman alleged that Berlanga “began hitting her with an open hand” and then “retrieved a pistol” and “struck her in the forehead” with the handle end of the weapon. The woman was then able to escape and take refuge in a local convenience store before the police arrived. The report further claimed that the woman then went to a local health care clinic for medical attention, where the responding officer noticed “swelling and bruising on her forehead” caused by Berlanga, along with a torn shirt and “an apparent bruise on her left inner arm.” As per court records, Berlanga appeared at the Bartow Courthouse on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026, where his bond was set at $16,000. His next court appearance is an arraignment hearing Nov. 17, 2026. With Zuffa Boxing, Berlanga is a veteran boxer and has fought several top names, including Canelo Alvarez . item.title: 2027: INEC moves to address electoral risks in Ebonyi
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Ebonyi State has intensified efforts to identify and address potential risks that could disrupt the conduct of the 2027 general elections. The move followed a workshop on Electoral Risk Management organised at the commission’s headquarters in Abakaliki for stakeholders, including media representatives, security agencies and local government electoral officers. Participants identified potential threats to the elections, including snatching and destruction of electoral materials, abduction of election officials and the inaccessibility of some villages and communities. Speaking at the workshop, INEC Administrative Secretary in Ebonyi State, Mrs Joan Onyibor, said the exercise was timely given the proximity of the January and February 2027 elections. She explained that electoral risk management provided a structured and proactive approach to identifying, assessing, monitoring and mitigating threats that could compromise the electoral process. According to her, such risks could include security threats, political tensions, misinformation, environmental challenges, logistical constraints and other operational difficulties. Onyibor warned that failure to identify and address the risks could disrupt electoral activities, endanger voters and election officials, and undermine public confidence in the electoral process. Declaring the workshop open, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Ebonyi State, Mrs Pauline Ugochi Onyeka, commended the Head of Planning and Monitoring, Mrs Mercy Amechi-Okorie, for organising the programme for stakeholders. Onyeka said strengthening the electoral risk management framework had become increasingly important as the 2027 elections approached. “We must move beyond responding to challenges only after they emerge and adopt a proactive approach that allows us to anticipate risks and address them before they develop into serious threats,” she said. She added that the workshop was designed to improve stakeholders’ understanding of electoral risk management, build institutional capacity and strengthen their ability to identify, document and report potential threats across different locations. The REC stressed that effective electoral risk management depended on close cooperation and timely information-sharing among INEC offices, security agencies, civil society organisations, the media and other stakeholders. “No institution can manage every electoral risk effectively on its own,” Onyeka said, calling for a coordinated approach to strengthen preparedness and response mechanisms. She said collaboration among stakeholders would help improve the security and integrity of the electoral process ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Tunji Olowolafe Charts Three Strategies for Research Excellence at OAU at 65
item.description: At the Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Ile-Ife 65th anniversary celebration, Dr. Tunji Olowolafe , Founder of the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation (TOF) , called on Nigerian universities to open research to more people, test long-held beliefs with scientific rigour and carry discoveries out of the laboratory and into the economy. Speaking on the theme, Promoting Research Excellence and Innovation in Postgraduate Studies: Charting the Future, Dr. Olowolafe reframed research as the disciplined habit of correcting a nation’s course based on evidence. He described the postgraduate college as the intellectual engine room of a nation, where society sends its sharpest minds to challenge conventional wisdom and demand honest, data-driven answers. His first strategy called for opening the gates of research earlier, wider and more flexibly. He urged OAU to make its Staff Schools benchmarks for Africa, with science, technology and artificial intelligence at the core of the curriculum. He pointed to the Foundation’s Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial Community Secondary School in Are-Ekiti, which opened in September 2025 with 100 students and now has more than 170, alongside an ICT centre teaching artificial intelligence, coding, graphic design and Mandarin, with instructors teaching live from Beijing through a Starlink connection. “The postgraduate researchers of 2040 are sitting in primary classrooms today,” he said. He also questioned whether every road to postgraduate research must run through a four-year degree, inviting universities to recognize prior learning and demonstrated expertise without lowering standards. With only about one million of the two million UTME candidates admitted in 2025, he argued that flexible, digital study must become the standard model, since a digital campus needs no physical acreage. This builds on the Foundation’s Project Digi-Teach, which is training academic staff at Ekiti State University (EKSU) for digital proficiency. His second strategy urged researchers to test what society believes. Rather than dismissing indigenous knowledge without investigation or defending it without validation, he called for rigorous testing, citing Chinese scientist Tu Youyou , whose study of a centuries-old herbal remedy produced the malaria treatment artemisinin and a Nobel Prize. He extended the same principle to national history, including sensitive chapters such as the Civil War. “She neither rejected tradition nor accepted it. She tested it,” he said. The third strategy focused on pushing research out of the laboratory and directly into the economy. Dr. Olowolafe advocated university promotion structures that reward patents, commercial products and solved industrial problems alongside traditional journal publications. “Research is complete only when it leaves the laboratory and improves lives,” he said. item.title: Husker Wrestle-Offs: Here’s What You Need to Know Going into Saturday, and Yes It’s Open to the Public
item.description: Incoming transfer Vincent Robinson, seen here at the 2026 NCAA Championships wrestling for NC State, will take on some talented young wrestlers at 125 pounds Saturday in the Nebraska wrestling room. | NCAA Photos via Getty Images Nebraska will hold its annual preseason wrestle-offs Saturday in the Husker wrestling room. While some of the weights are foregone conclusions, there are a number of weights with a lot of question marks. The event starts Saturday at 3:30 p.m. and will be open to the public — it will be located on the top floor of the Hendricks Training Complex on the south end of the Bob Devaney Sports Center. Fans should park in Lot 58 on the east side of the Devaney Center. Join us next Saturday in the wrestling room for our 2026 wrestle-offs. Fans can park in Lot 58 on the east side of the Devaney Sports Center. pic.twitter.com/Mo3uSyoAAl — Nebraska Wrestling (@HuskerWrestling) October 22, 2026 The brackets and even some of the weight classes are not known, but I did my best to give my prediction for what this weekend’s brackets may look like: If I had to guess, this is what I think the brackets for the @HuskerWrestling wrestle-offs could look like this Saturday 125 pounds – 149 pounds pic.twitter.com/q0t3UEszbV — Dylan Guenther (@DguenthWrestle) October 28, 2026 With ten true freshmen on the roster, there are some questions as to where some of them land weight-class wise this season, so don’t be surprised if some of these guys wrestle this weekend at different weight classes than I predicted. Onto my thoughts… Weight-By-Weight Notes 125 pounds — With the addition of NCAA Champion Vincent Robinson through the transfer portal, it’s pretty well set that he’ll be Nebraska’s starter, but there are still some interesting questions at this weight. How does incoming freshman and Nebraska prep legend Zaiyahn Ornelas (4x state champ at Wilber-Clatonia and Creighton Prep) fair as a true freshman? Then there’s a potential matchup between fellow in-state legends Kael Lauridsen (4x state champion for Bennington) and Abdi Unle (2x state champ for Omaha Bryan) on the other side of the bracket. After starting last year, has Lauridsen made jumps? Same for Unle who is coming off a redshirt year. 133 pounds — In a classic senior vs. freshman matchup, Jacob Van Dee is the guy here but he’ll have his hands full with incoming freshman Elijah Collick, a four-time Maryland state champion. 141 pounds — This is THE BRACKET for Nebraska. Four wrestlers with at least four years of eligibility will all be competing for one spot. Jake Hockaday redshirted last year after winning four state titles in Indiana, while Omar Ayoub received a medical redshirt after breaking his hand early last season, giving him four years of eligibility remaining. Then there are true freshmen Lincoln Sledzianowski and Davis Parrow who are coming off illustrious high school careers and could challenge for the starting spot here. Honestly, I don’t know where Parrow will be come Saturday —

item.title: Kris Letang might still have some game left
item.description: PITTSBURGH, PA - OCTOBER 22: Pittsburgh Penguins defenseman Kris Letang (58) looks on during the second period in the NHL game between the Pittsburgh Penguins and the Florida Panthers on October 22, 2026, at PPG Paints Arena in Pittsburgh, PA. (Photo by Jeanine Leech/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Over the past couple of years, defenseman Kris Letang seemed to be the one member of the Pittsburgh Penguins big-three that had slowed down the most. Not only in terms of offensive production, but just general, overall impact. Father time was catching up, and the adjustment to that did not seem to be going well. There were even more signs of that over the first couple of games of the 2026-27 season. But over the past couple of weeks there are some encouraging signs that maybe Letang still has some game left, and that maybe he is adjusting to his new limitations and what he can and can not do. That has especially been the case since he has not been paired up with Trevor van Riemsdyk, an early-season pairing that just did not seem to click the way the Penguins might have hoped. While Letang has not really made a significant contribution offensively with just six asssists (and zero goals), his defensive impacts have been shockingly strong. fwiw here is what i have for defensive D https://t.co/f7wxpQNjYY pic.twitter.com/kUK5ZD8f3b — HockeyStatCards (@hockeystatcards) October 25, 2026 When he has been on the ice during 5-on-5 play, the Penguins have allowed just four goals in 198 minutes of hockey, and only 1.96 expected goals per 60 minutes. That expected goal number is the lowest among the team’s defensemen (minimum 100 minutes played), and the third-lowest of any player on the team (trailing only forwards Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte). Among 186 defensemen across the NHL, it is 11th. Those are promising numbers. The Penguins do have an extremely high save percentage with Letang on the ice (over .940) which is probably not a sustainable number, so there might be some additional goals against to come his way just through some regression, but the fact there are not a lot of chances being allowed is an encouraging sign that could help mitigate that somewhat. It is also eye-opening how much more effective he has been paired with literally any other defenseman on the roster outside of van Riemsdyk. There are some small sample sizes here with each of these pairings, but the overall performance is pretty consistent among the pairings. Pairing Minutes Played GF GA xGF/60 xGA/60 xGF% Kris Letang-Trevor van Riemsdyk 57.57 1 1 2.32 3.39 40.7 Kris Letang-Spencer Stastney 53.52 1 0 2.70 1.03 72.3 Kris Letang-Ilya Solovyov 36.58 1 0 1.61 1.49 51.9 Kris Letang-Sam Girard 16.27 0 2 3.23 1.59 67.0 Kris Letang-Declan Carlile 16.16 1 1 5.12 1.59 76.2 I am going to chalk this up to three things that are likely working in harmony here to produce these results. item.title: Does Daniel Ricciardo regret leaving Red Bull for Renault?
item.description: Motorsport photo Back in July 2018, Daniel Ricciardo was one of the most highly-rated drivers in the Formula 1 paddock. He had been in the Red Bull family for a decade, since his early junior single-seater career, and was now spearheading the brand’s effort in the world championship. But when Cyril Abiteboul came knocking with a Renault F1 deal, Ricciardo decided to make that bold switch, even though he had won two grands prix in the first half of the 2018 season while the yellow cars had failed to finish any better than fifth. The gamble didn’t pay off. Ricciardo failed to achieve a single podium finish in 2019, Renault was beaten to fourth by McLaren in the constructors’ championship, and he signed with the Woking-based outfit for 2021 even before the 2020 campaign got under way – having been delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic. Daniel Ricciardo, Renault F1 Team Daniel Ricciardo, Renault F1 Team The Australian tremendously struggled at McLaren, other than a shock victory in the 2021 Italian Grand Prix, so much that he didn’t see his contract out and was replaced by fellow countryman Oscar Piastri for the 2023 season. His fortunes did not improve in a final stint at his old AlphaTauri/RB team – which was cut short by his underperformance too. Meanwhile, former team-mate Max Verstappen kept rising and eventually took four consecutive world titles with the Red Bull squad Ricciardo had left of his own volition. Eight years on, when asked in the Beyond The Grid podcast if he regretted leaving Red Bull, Ricciardo pondered: “I still don’t really know how to answer it, because I definitely don’t want to say, ‘Oh, yeah, I would have been world champion if I stayed’, because it’s not a reality that was lived. Max has gone on to prove he is one of the best ever, so I don’t want to dismiss that as well and be like, ‘Yeah, I would have beat Max and become world champion’. It wouldn’t have been an easy task, but I think it’s also maybe a bit unfair towards him to say that. Obviously I respect him a lot. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, congratulates pole man Daniel Ricciardo, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, congratulates pole man Daniel Ricciardo, Red Bull Racing “I acknowledge definitely that it was a decision that was… If I tell you everything that went on, it was wild.” What drove Ricciardo’s decision was, in part, a need for change, after that decade in the Red Bull fold. “If I’m to answer it shortly, yes, I wish I would have stayed, but… I don’t know, at the time, I left because I felt I was getting a bit comfortable, a bit complacent,” he continued. “I think there was a desire to try something else. It’s not that black and white. “If I could have been a world champion, was that my best opportunity? Yes, absolutely. I would have loved to have known another reality of if I stayed. I don’t want to say it haunts me, but it’s the one unknown that I’m like, ‘Hmm, I’m so interested how that would have panned out’.” Daniel Ricciardo, Renault F1 T

item.title: The differences between Spalletti and Carrick amid Conte speculation
item.description: The differences between Spalletti and Carrick amid Conte speculation Antonio Conte has been linked with both Juventus and Manchester United; while neither club is reportedly in advanced talks with the Italian tactician, the Red Devils appear closer than the Bianconeri to making a managerial change. Juventus and Manchester United are both enduring difficult periods in Serie A and the Premier League, respectively, and speculation around Antonio Conte is another point of common ground between the two clubs. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Fabrizio Romano provided the latest updates on the Italian tactician on his YouTube channel, highlighting the main differences between Juventus and Manchester United’s situations. ITALY – OCTOBER 21: Michael Carrick, Manager of Manchester United, at half time during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Italy. item.title: Predicting ACC football scores in Week 9: North Carolina looks for upset bid vs. Miami
item.description: Both Week 7 and Week 8 were wild weeks in college football . Will Week 9 have similar results? It’s quite possible with all the upsets we’ve witnessed in recent weeks. As for the ACC, there are a couple of games worth tuning into this week to see if there are upsets. The big game will come in the evening when the top-ranked Hurricanes travel to North Carolina to take on the Tar Heels. Bill Belichick’s team has played much better than anyone expected, but will the Tar Heels have the gas to keep up with Miami? Both ranked SMU and Wake Forest will look to stay alive with games against Syracuse and Virginia, respectively. Here’s how every ACC game might play out in Week 9. item.title: Packers’ perfect Tony Pollard trade offer to Titans before NFL trade deadline
item.description: Packers’ perfect Tony Pollard trade offer to Titans before NFL trade deadline appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Green Bay Packers may not know it, but they have a Jordan Love problem hiding in plain sight. Their QB is carrying an offense that cannot consistently move the ball on the ground. Tony Pollard could help change that equation. The Tennessee Titans running back has the burst, versatility, and proven production to give Matt LaFleur’s offense another dimension. Now, Tennessee’s difficult season could create an opportunity for Green Bay to strike. With the trade deadline approaching, general manager Brian Gutekunst should explore a deal that addresses an obvious weakness without sacrificing the Packers’ long-term flexibility. Backfield spark needed Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Through seven weeks, the Packers have stumbled their way to a 4-3 record. They have mixed impressive victories with frustrating inconsistency. They opened with a loss to Minnesota, edged the New York Jets, and absorbed a home defeat against Atlanta. That was before recovering with wins over Tampa Bay, Chicago, and Dallas. Their three-game winning streak ended in a painful 20-17 loss to Detroit. In that game, Green Bay had opportunities to take control but failed to finish. The bigger concern now is the running game. Green Bay averaged fewer than 60 rushing yards per game through its first seven contests. That has left Love and the passing attack with too much responsibility. Josh Jacobs returned against Detroit, but his 36 rushing yards on 11 carries did little to solve the problem . Injuries along the offensive line have added another complication . Jacobs can still be a major contributor, but Green Bay needs more reliable explosiveness and depth as the schedule tightens. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Pry Tony Pollard Pollard is a logical target. He can contribute as both a runner and receiver. The 29-year-old has 478 rushing yards, averages 4.3 yards per carry, and has scored four rushing touchdowns through seven games in 2026. His latest performance was particularly eye-catching. Pollard rushed for 129 yards and three touchdowns against Cleveland. That demonstrated that he could still take over a game when the blocking and opportunities are there. The Titans, meanwhile, are 1-6 and facing difficult questions about their direction. If Tennessee decides to prioritize future draft capital, Pollard could become a valuable trade deadline asset. That makes him a potential rental, which should keep the asking price reasonable. Gutekunst’s ideal proposal would be a 2027 fourth-round pick and a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick for Pollard. The later selection could improve to a fifth-rounder if Pollard reaches an agreed-upon rushing or scrimmage-yardage threshold. For Tennessee, that package would provide future draft flexibility. For the Packers, it would be a measured investment

item.title: ‘He still has a lot to prove’: Waqar Younis makes bold claim on Jasprit Bumrah
item.description: Former Pakistan captain Waqar Younis has hailed Jasprit Bumrah as the standout bowler in modern-day white-ball cricket but believes the Indian fast bowler still has more to establish in the Test format. Despite Bumrah's impressive record of 234 wickets in 52 Tests at an average of 19.7 and a strike rate of 42.8, Waqar feels the pacer has not played enough red-ball cricket to be placed ahead of other leading fast bowlers. “There’s no modern-day bowler of the same calibre as Bumrah with the white ball. Leave out Test cricket. He still has a lot to prove in Tests; he hasn’t played as much. There are plenty of others, like Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. You can’t ignore some of the English bowlers either. But when you talk about T20 and one-day cricket, I feel that in terms of impact, Bumrah always delivers in crunch scenarios. And that’s what matters,” Waqar said on the Shubhankar Mishra podcast. Waqar's assessment comes despite Bumrah's significant achievements in the longest format. The India pacer became the fastest Indian fast bowler to reach 50 Test wickets in 2018, accomplishing the milestone in his 11th match. He went on to claim his 100th Test wicket in his 24th appearance. Bumrah also became only the third Indian bowler to take a Test hat-trick in 2019. His performances in 2024 earned him the ICC Men's Test Cricketer of the Year award, while he finished the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy with 32 wickets in five Tests, a record haul for the series. The right-arm pacer has also been highly effective in England, taking 51 wickets in 11 Tests. One possible reason behind Waqar's assessment is Bumrah's limited availability in Test cricket compared with Australian quicks Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. Injuries and workload management have affected his participation, and he is yet to play a Test for India this year. Bumrah is expected to return for India's two-match Test series in New Zealand next month, with a place in the World Test Championship final at stake. Waqar recalls Bumrah's match-winning spell against Pakistan While questioning Bumrah's standing in Tests, Waqar was unequivocal about the Indian pacer's influence in ODIs and T20Is. He particularly remembered Bumrah's decisive contribution in India's six-run victory over Pakistan at the 2024 T20 World Cup in New York. Pakistan appeared firmly in control at 80/3 after 14 overs, needing only 40 runs from the final six overs to chase India's target of 120. Bumrah dismissed Mohammad Rizwan, triggering a collapse that helped India defend the modest total. Waqar believes that spell demonstrated why Bumrah is such a valuable asset in high-pressure situations, particularly when a captain needs a breakthrough. “Whenever an India captain is in trouble, he always gives the ball to Bumrah. Pakistan had no business losing in New York. The required rate was well under control. That over in which Bumrah dismissed Rizwan proved to be the difference. Impact players are the key players. item.title: 2026-27 WCC Men’s Basketball Preview
item.description: Mar 20, 2026; St. Louis, MO, USA; Santa Clara Broncos guard Jake Ensminger (44) walks onto the court before a first round game of the men's 2026 NCAA Tournament against the Kentucky Wildcats at Enterprise Center. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Le-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s a new era for the WCC. Not only is Gonzaga now in the Pac 12, but Saint Mary’s lost longtime head coach Randy Bennett to Arizona State. While the Gaels are still in the league and will be a contender, the conference is certainly more open than it has been in recent years at the top. It may not get three bids like it did last year, but it won’t be a foregone conclusion who is getting a bid on opening night. 1. Santa Clara Assuming Elijah Mahi is eligible, I’d have the Broncos as the top team in the WCC to open the season, but only by a hair. Mahi puts them over the top, having averaged 14.1 points and 4.7 rebounds per game last year, and is primed for even more this year. Jake Ensminger and Sash Gavalyugov are back, with Gavalyugov needing to be much more consistent to have a breakout season. The Broncos also always seem to have a breakout newcomer, and Sidi Gueye fits the bill for me as an athletic 6-foot-10 sophomore transfer from Arizona. 2. Saint Mary’s The ever-consistent Saint Mary’s program has as much change as ever this year with Mickey McConnell replacing Randy Bennett. McConnell will keep the program in contention, but I don’t think they’re quite at the NCAA Tournament home-whites caliber that we’ve come to expect from the Gaels. SMC returns point guard Joshua Dent and should get a big leap from wing Mantas Juzenas. Freshman guard Darius Bivins is probably the most talented rookie in the league. But the frontcourt raises questions. There’s no returning beacon of consistency in that group. Somebody needs to step up big – likely one of Thomas Ndong, Vangelis Zougris or Salih Altuntas – if the Gaels are going to remain at-large caliber. 3. Pepperdine I’ve written all summer about how much I like this Pepperdine team. Griff Aldrich took Longwood to the NCAA Tournament twice and then built a really strong roster for year one in Malibu. A frontcourt with legit size and shot-blocking from Xavier transfer Anthony Robinson, and some dribble-pass-shoot elements from Long Beach State transfer Petar Majstorovic should be good in this league. Evan Haywood and Jahari Williamson can each be some of the best shooters in this conference, while Will McClendon is the straw that stirs the drink. And then, freshman Alex Constanza, along with a fascinating international recruiting class provides a big ceiling as well. 4. Pacific Dave Smart’s Pacific team jumped up 172 spots in KenPom in his second season, finishing 112 last year. In his third season, he has the ceiling hinging on a few five-in-five cases. item.title: Here's why Charlie Woods' dramatic 40-foot birdie putt on the 18th hole was momentous
item.description: Charlie Woods saved his best shot for last. The son of Tiger Woods , who plays for the Benjamin School in Palm Beach, Florida, drained a 40-foot birdie putt on the 18th hole Tuesday to shoot a 2-under 69 and claim medalist honors in the Class 1A-District 14 championship at Champions Club at Summerfield in Stuart, Florida. The dramatic finish gave Woods the individual title by one shot over teammate Brooks Colton and helped Benjamin take another step toward defending its Florida boys golf state championship. The Buccaneers shot 290, beating runner-up Oxbridge Academy by 15 strokes. "We got two good rounds out of Charlie and Brooks," Benjamin coach Toby Harbeck told the Palm Beach Post . "Charlie made a 40-foot putt on the last hole to win the individual title. Charlie shot a 69 and Brooks shot a 70. That's what you want out of your No. 1 and No. 2." More: Inside Tiger Woods’ potential comeback: What Golfweek has learned about his return Woods made birdies at Nos. 4, 10, 13 and 18 and played the other 14 holes in 2 over. Colton's 1-under 70 included an eagle at the par-5 fourth. Woods is scheduled to play at Florida State next fall, joining the top-ranked prospect in the Class of 2027, Miles Russell, in the Seminoles' recruiting class. The performance continued a strong fall for Woods and Benjamin. At the Palm League Championship in September at Biltmore Golf Course Miami, Woods shot an even-par 71 and finished eighth individually as the Buccaneers rallied on the back nine to win the team championship. Andrew Tsar, an SMU commit, earned medalist honors with a 2-under 69. "It played really hard, long, and windy and rainy," Harbeck said of the district event. "It was everything. So, I'm very pleased. You're trying to move on each week and get to the finals, so that's what we did. We've got to keep going forward." Tim Schmitt is the managing editor of Golfweek and the golf coordinator for the USA Today Network. item.title: Dillon Mitchell on how he, Chris Cenac Jr. finding niche with Boston Celtics
item.description: It can be tough to be a top recruit heading into college, get drafted, and then find yourself on the bottom rung of a roster after years at the top wherever you were playing. But that is the story for many if not most players making the transition to the NBA from the NCAA ranks, and success in the Association can often depend on how well that adjustment goes. And both of the Boston Celtics selections from the 2026 NBA Draft are going through this themselves, with Chris Cenac Jr. and Dillon Mitchell both doing a good job adapting to their developmental role with Boston. The latter had some words for how he and Cenac Jr. have managed to find their niche with their new team in a recent interview . "I know mainly for both of us as rookies, nobody's expecting us to come in here and score all these buckets or do all these things," said Mitchell. "It's the little things, and that's how we're going to be able to play," he added. "That's how we're going to be able to make an impact for the Celtics, rebounding, being the best defensive playmakers we can on the team, being listeners, communicating on defense." "So a lot of it is not about scoring or anything offensively. A lot of it is defense and your effort and your hustle, and that's the main things they preach and we focus on." And it should serve them well as they grow into larger roles with Boston in the future. item.title: Former Gunner announces retirement at 33
item.description: Former Gunner announces retirement at 33 Former Arsenal striker Chuks Aneke has announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 33. Photo by Tony Marshall/Getty Images Posting on social media on Wednesday, former Gunner Chuks Aneke revealed that he’s retiring from his playing days. “I’d like to officially announce my retirement from professional football,” Aneke wrote on Instagram . “Also like to express my gratitude to all the coaches all the staff, my teachers, my friends and my family and the fans, the ones who supported me and the ones who’s didn’t. “It was all part of an amazing journey and I wouldn’t change it. Looking forward to the Second Half.” Photo by Victor Fraile/Getty Images Aneke played for the Arsenal academy from the age of seven all the way through to the first-team, making his senior debut in a League Cup win over Shrewsbury in 2011. That senior appearance was folllowed by a few loan spells, with Aneke playing for Stevenage , Preston North End , and Crewe Alexandra . The striker was then released and moved to the Belgian Pro League with Zulte Waregem . But he returned to England a couple of years later, spending the remainder of his career with the MK Dons , Charlton Athletic , Birmingham City , and Shrewsbury Town . Photo by Jacques Feeney/Getty Images Aneke’s retirement had been hinted at earlier this year, with Shrewsbury confirming that the player had stepped away from his playing duties to work with the club’s recruitment department. But he hadn’t officially confirmed his retirement until now. Aneke had plenty of career highlights, beginning with his youth accolades of winning the Premier Academy League with Arsenal and the u17 Euros with England . At senior level, Aneke won the EFL Trophy with Crewe Alexandra in 2012, and he achieved promotions to League One with MK Dons and to the Championship with Charlton. Given he scored 19 goals in the MK Dons’ promotion campaign, the forward could arguably call that his best individual season. We wish the former Gunner the best with whatever’s next in his career. Photo by Bryn Lennon/Getty Images

item.title: Game-by-game predictions for Alabama's remaining 2026 schedule
item.description: Having entered their bye week sitting at 6-2 overall (4-2 SEC), every game going forward is essentially considered a must-win for the Alabama Crimson Tide , and it's not hard to see why. A team with College Football Playoff (CFP) aspirations, Alabama enters November with two losses on their resume, having fallen to both Georgia and Tennessee in previous weeks. As a result, the Crimson Tide cannot afford to drop a third game in the regular season, as it could potentially be detrimental to their CFP chances. Looking ahead, Alabama will enter the homestretch of their regular season schedule coming out of the bye, starting with a challenging road matchup in Week 10. That will be the first-of-four games remaining on Alabama's regular season schedule, with two others also set to come against SEC foes. Here are those four games remaining on Alabama's regular season schedule, as well as an early prediction for each. Week 10: at LSU Tigers When: Saturday, Nov. 7, in Baton Rouge, Louisiana Prediction: Alabama 24, LSU 26 Alabama's upcoming Week 10 road game at LSU is undoubtedly their toughest remaining regular season contest on paper, one that could essentially serve as a potential CFP elimination game for both teams. Recently opening as the underdog in Baton Rouge, Alabama will be faced with a challenging test against LSU and head coach Lane Kiffin, as the Tigers have an offense that ranks top 10 nationally in scoring, led by the SEC's leading passer Sam Leavitt. Week 11: at Vanderbilt Commodores When: Saturday, Nov. 14, in Nashville, Tennessee Prediction: Alabama 40, Vanderbilt 17 Alabama is set to travel to Nashville on Nov. 14 for the first time since the Crimson Tide were stunned by Vanderbilt in Kalen DeBoer's first season. The Commodores have struggled this season with an offense and defense that both rank in the 100's nationally, and it's simply hard to see Alabama falling in Nashville this season, even despite their struggles there in 2024. Week 12: vs. Chattanooga Mocs When: Saturday, Nov. 21, in Tuscaloosa, Alabama Prediction: Alabama 63, Chattanooga 6 Alabama's final nonconference regular season game comes at home in Week 12 against Chattanooga. The Crimson Tide will likely win big over the Mocs, a FCS team, at home. Week 13: vs. Auburn Tigers When: Saturday, Nov. 28, in Tuscaloosa, Alabama Prediction: Alabama 36, Auburn 20 Alabama's regular season schedule will come to a close in Tuscaloosa with a Week 13 showdown against Auburn in the latest edition of the Iron Bowl. The Tigers' first under head coach Alex Golesh, this will be a tough matchup, as always, and while Auburn did recently upset Georgia in Athens, they have been inconsistent this season, making it tough to pick against an Alabama team that was won the last seven Iron Bowl's played in Tuscaloosa. item.title: Wales wing Adams released for Cardiff at Ospreys
item.description: Josh Adams started for Wales against Fiji and Argentina in July [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Wales wing Josh Adams has been released from international camp to start for Cardiff against Ospreys at St Helen's in the United Rugby Championship (URC). item.title: Coaching Concerns and Injury Woes Are Catching Up to the Kings
item.description: Oct 23, 2026; Sacramento, California, USA; Sacramento Kings head coach Doug Christie reacts after a play against the Portland Trail Blazers during the first quarter at Golden 1 Center. Mandatory Credit: Dennis Lee-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Benjamin Yu, Editor Only four games into the 2026-27 NBA season, the Sacramento Kings are starting to look familiar. Currently 0-4, the Kings’ bad start demonstrates a struggle for consistency, despite injuries that have weakened their rotation. Although the issue of injuries is something that may derail any team’s season, the concerns currently plaguing the Kings also cast doubt on the ability of the coaches to adapt when things start going poorly. For the Kings, this problem seems familiar from last year. Injuries Have Weakened The Rotation The Kings entered the new season missing key bench pieces, specifically Maxime Raynaud and Dylan Cardwell , both injured in preseason games and unable to play when the regular season began. In addition, Malik Monk was also unavailable for Sacramento’s season opener against the LA Clippers due to an injury. It’s tough when several key players get hurt before the season starts, especially when the team needs time to build chemistry and establish an identity. The biggest concern is that Sacramento’s injury problems will continue before they can find a consistent pace. It is even harder for Keegan Murray because his recurring ankle issues keep disrupting his progress and availability. After struggling with ankle issues last season and undergoing offseason surgery, Murray seemed poised to overcome them. Still, he has now experienced yet another episode of pain at the start of the new season. It has kept Murray out of action and denied Sacramento its multi-positional defender, perimeter shooter, and scorer who doesn’t always need the ball. Oct 10, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Sacramento Kings forward Keegan Murray (13) shoots over Golden State Warriors guard Brandin Podziemski (2) during the first quarter at Chase Center. Mandatory Credit: Justine Willard-Imagn Images Poor Coaching Is Weighing The Team Down Even though the injuries are certainly a concern, they are no excuse for all the problems Sacramento has had in the first four games of the season. There are concerns about the choices Doug Christie and his coaching staff have made in lineup decisions and in-game adjustments, as well as in recognizing certain matchups. Another problem is finding the right balance between developing the young star , Darius Acuff , and giving him the chance to shed light on the one skill that sets him apart . It is never easy to handle, especially when you’re competing at the same time. These issues are particularly frustrating because they aren’t new. They came up before with Christie during last year’s season, when he coached the team, and we discussed lineup issues, matchups, and accountability for the team’s problems. item.title: Dragons' depth test against Zebre amid Wales calls
item.description: Angus O'Brien is set for his first Dragons start of the season [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Dragons will attempt to showcase their deeper squad by avoiding a Zebre banana skin despite a long injury list and Wales absentees. Filo Tiatia's men end the first block of the season against the winless Italians in the United Rugby Championship (URC) at Rodney Parade on Saturday (17:30 GMT). Dragons do so without their five members of Wales' Nations Championship squad - centre Aneurin Owen, scrum-half Che Hope, tight-head prop Dillon Lewis and locks Ben Carter and Seb Davies. Wing Rio Dyer was a sixth player to get the initial call-up, but he was released after a hamstring strain suffered in defeat by Ospreys last weekend. He is on a 12-strong injury list, but co-captain Angus O'Brien, himself back from a leg niggle, is confident Dragons will cope. "We've developed competition right throughout the squad over the past couple of years," said the full-back. "We want as many boys in that Wales set-up as possible and it's really exciting to see those names in there because they have worked their socks off. "For those of us playing at the weekend it's about stepping up, and feel confident we have the ability across the squad to do that." Wales call up in-form Page after Dyer injury blow Where are Wales internationals really made? The result against Zebre will determine whether Dragons' first block of the season can be considered solid or a disappointment. They started with a draw at Benetton and have since played four fixtures in Wales, beating Scarlets in the URC and Perpignan in the Challenge Cup in Newport. Ospreys won at Rodney Parade and completed a double when winning 31-14 in horrendous conditions at the revamped St Helen's last Saturday. That was Dragons' first poor performance of the season and a response is needed against a Zebre team who have not won in the URC since 5 October, 2025. Tiatia's side won twice in Parma in April when they backed up a Challenge Cup quarter-final victory with a last-minute league success. "Zebre's results don't reflect their performances. They are a dogged side who are difficult to put away," said attack coach Matt O'Brien. "They play some expansive rugby and it will be a challenge, but hopefully we can repeat the results from last season." If Dragons win with a try bonus then they will be halfway towards last season's tally of 28 points. Influential prop Hunt has surgery Robert Hunt joined Dragons from Cheetahs in 2025 [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Dragons are assessing the extent of Dyer's hamstring injury but are set to be without tight-head prop Robert Hunt until the New Year after he had an operation on his left elbow. The South African suffered the injury at a scrum in the defeat by Ospreys in Newport on 9 October. With Lewis on Wales duty, Chris Coleman starts against Zebre with 21-year-old Owain James on the bench. item.title: William Contreras and Pat Murphy share emotional moment after Brewers win World Series
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers have reached a milestone decades in the making, capturing their first World Series title with a 4-1 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 5 of the 2026 championship series. After falling short in their only previous appearance in 1982, Pat Murphy, William Contreras and co. finally got another shot at the crown and made it count. More than four decades of waiting have led to this moment, proving that sometimes the greatest rewards come to those who refuse to give up. William Contreras y manager Pat Murphy. Eso es todo, amigos. pic.twitter.com/jyJDeuQ9i0 — Enrique Rojas/ESPN (@Enrique_Rojas1) October 29, 2026 The emotion surrounding Milwaukee’s long awaited championship was clear in the embrace between star catcher William Contreras and manager Pat Murphy after the Brewers sealed their Game 5 victory over the Rays. Their heartfelt moment captured what the title meant to a team that had spent years chasing the ultimate prize. William Contreras with the Brewers Oct 28, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski (32) and catcher William Contreras (24) react during the sixth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game five of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images William Contreras knows how painful postseason elimination can be after spending several years as a key part of Milwaukee’s roster. Since joining the Brewers’ core in 2023, he endured back to back Wild Card exits before suffering another setback when the Los Angeles Dodgers swept Milwaukee in the 2025 NLCS. After those repeated disappointments, finally winning it all made the championship even more meaningful. Even as the Milwaukee Brewers reshaped its roster over multiple seasons, the Brewers never lost sight of their goal, with William Contreras becoming one of the team’s most dependable figures along the way. Behind the plate, he takes charge of the pitching staff and helps carry out Pat Murphy’s game plan , acting as the manager’s trusted voice on the field. Oct 12, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Brewers catcher William Contreras (24) celebrates after defeating the Los Angeles Dodgers in game two of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images Their shared embrace after the final out carried extra meaning, as both finally celebrated a championship after years of pursuing one. Milwaukee’s championship run would not have been possible without William Contreras’ MVP caliber contributions and Pat Murphy’s leadership throughout the season. Both have played crucial roles in bringing the franchise its long awaited title, and they have every reason to savor the celebrations ahead. Their achievements have secured them a lasting place in baseball history. item.title: Dave Pasch reflects on difficult decision to leave Cardinals for ESPN’s NFL booth
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports It took Dave Pasch a single Sunday on the couch to realize he had been running on fumes for most of a quarter century. Pasch told Jimmy Traina on the Traina Thoughts podcast that leaving the Arizona Cardinals radio booth was painful, even with a national NFL opportunity waiting for him in Bristol. The longtime play-by-play voice signed a multiyear extension with ESPN in June that expanded his portfolio to include the NFL, and taking that assignment meant surrendering the Cardinals job he held for 24 seasons. He now leads one of two NFL Network booths under ESPN’s control, working alongside Kurt Warner and Jason Kelce . “It was really tough, Jimmy. It was a job that I really enjoyed,” Pasch said. “Obviously, the team did not have great success with the exception of maybe a handful of years. In those 24 years, I had the same partner for 20 years, Ron Wolfley. And then this past year, I worked with A.Q. Shipley, who’s really good, and really enjoyed that. That was the best part of last year because it was really a bad year for the team.” Wolfley, a former Cardinals fullback, joined the radio broadcast in 2004 after first interviewing for the analyst job when Pasch took over play-by-play, and his raucous, locker-room enthusiasm became the perfect foil for Pasch’s steadier delivery. That partnership concluded when Wolfley stepped down after 20 seasons ahead of the 2025 campaign, though he retained his local midday show and weekly Cardinals program. The franchise then consulted Pasch as it weighed potential successors before settling on A.Q. Shipley that July. The new pairing survived only one season, and Shipley now shares the booth with J.P. Shadrick , whom the Cardinals hired in August to replace Pasch as the team’s radio voice. “And you know, Michael Bidwill, the owner, had been really good to me over the years,” Pasch added. “And ESPN had been good to me in terms of trying to work around my schedule the best it could with college football.” For most of his Cardinals tenure, Pasch answered to two employers every weekend. His Saturdays went to ESPN’s college football coverage, most recently alongside analyst Dusty Dvoracek and sideline reporter Taylor McGregor , and the itinerant autumns turned Pasch and Dvoracek into hotel-room movie buddies who unwound with James Bond films and Airplane! between assignments. His Sundays went to Arizona, regardless of how many connecting flights and rental cars stood between the two. The conclusion of football season never brought much respite, either, since the extension he signed in June kept him on ESPN’s NBA and college basketball coverage, where he has called games beside Hubie Brown and Doris Burke . “So again, I wasn’t looking to leave, but you know, when ESPN offers you the opportunity to do NFL and all the other things were in place, it was great,” he said. item.description: ‘He could be late 30s or whatever’: Tim Seifert in awe of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s fearless batting, ‘unbelievable’ skill set at 15 originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: New Zealand opener Tim Seifert says Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hits like a man in his late thirties. India made the fastest team hundred in men’s T20Is, getting there in five overs. Sooryavanshi hammered 45 off 19 balls in Wellington, helping India reach 133 for one. Beyond his years! Tim Seifert marvels at Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s amazing skill set Tim Seifert has admitted he is left stunned by the power and fearlessness of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, a batter who is only 15 years old and yet strikes the ball with the authority of a seasoned veteran. The New Zealand opener made his feelings known after watching the youngster tear into the home attack during the third T20I in Wellington. India put together a remarkable batting display on Tuesday, October 27, and a string of T20I records fell during their chase. Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma were the main architects of that explosive start, and together they gave the visitors a platform that left the New Zealand bowlers overwhelmed. The Men in Blue took only five overs to bring up the fastest team hundred in men’s T20Is, which is a new benchmark for the format. They also matched the record for the quickest team fifty, getting there in 2.2 overs, and posted the highest team score ever seen in the first six overs of a men’s T20I innings. MORE: India vs New Zealand 4th T20I predicted playing XI BCCI/Creimas Although Abhishek led the charge, Sooryavanshi complemented his senior and smashed 45 off just 19 balls, leaving India on 133/1. Seifert was speaking on The Agenda podcast. He began by dismissing the idea that Sooryavanshi’s age should matter at all. In his view, the way the teenager connects with the ball makes him look far older than he is. “Look, 15, he’s whatever age he is; the way that he hits the ball, he could be late 30s or whatever. The age is a little bit irrelevant. He is an amazing player." He then pointed to what he had seen first-hand at the IPL this year, where Sooryavanshi hit more sixes than anyone ever has in a single edition. “I was at the IPL this year and he got the most sixes ever, I think it was 70-odd or something like that. His age being 15, but the skill set that he has is unbelievable, and just the fearless cricket, as we saw the other night, it’s kind of how the generation is at the moment,” Seifert added. item.title: MLB offseason dates to remember
item.description: Dec 9, 2025; Orlando, FL, USA; General view of the press conference room during the 2025 MLB Winter Meetings at Signia by Hilton Hotel. Mandatory Credit: Mike Watters-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The World Series is over and there is a new champion among us. The Brewers have hoisted a piece of metal the Commissioner’s Trophy and are champions of the world. That means the offseason is here. With this offseason, there are certain dates to remember that are important on the baseball calendar. Here is a list of those dates: Free agent filing – day after World Series ends : by the time you read this, there is likely a flood of newly released players looking for work Free agency begins – five days after the World Series ends : teams have a five day window to make their final case to keep a player, but on this date, free agents can now talk to anyone they desire November 9-12 – GM Meetings in Las Vegas : the groundwork will be laid for many a deal to be made (wow, a poet and didn’t know it) November 17-19 – Owners meetings in New York : maybe a last ditch effort at making a surprise deal with the MLBPA and calling off the impending lockout November 17 – Deadline for players to accept the Qualifying Offer (4 pm ET), Rule 5 protection deadline (Players need to be added to 40-man roster to protect from the Rule 5 draft) : this is kind of a big deal as we don’t really know what the post-CBA agreement landscape will look like. Will there even be a Rule 5 draft any longer? Will qualifying offers be a thing? November 20 – Non-tender Deadline : Brandon Marsh, you up? December 1 – CBA Expires 11:59 pm ET : Listen, as optimistic as I am that a deal will get done that doesn’t really miss too much time, this is the big one. This is when the lockout begins where owners, who don’t actually have to do this, will lock out the players from team properties. Again, this doesn’t have to happen , but we all know that it will as a “negotiating tactic”. December 7-9 – Winter Meetings in San Diego : Yeah, this isn’t happening December 8 – Draft Lottery : Neither is this December 9 – Rule 5 Draft : This, if it is still a thing, will probably happen at a later date, but in December. Nah. January 8 – Arbitration Figures Exchanged : I cannot wait for the post-lockout scramble to happen, but that is when this will all go down. You can probably expect hearings for arbitration to come fast and furious once arbitration is settled and possibly revamped. January 15 – International Signing Period opens : I have questions about this. I’ll assume this still happens, but will anyone sign players considering an international draft is something that will be on the negotiating table? If it does happen, I wonder if that will be an indicator how negotiations are actually going. Most everything that is going on this offseason centers around the CBA negotiations. Until that is settled, we won’t see much of anything happening, but at least you are prepared for when it does.

So I wanted to have Joey on the show to help break down what this document tells us, both about Anthropic’s finances and the broader AI economy. item.title: Ghostly Cat’s Head Nebula lurks within sight of Hubble and Webb
item.description: The NASA/ESA Hubble and the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescopes recently stared at an eerie star-forming scene within the Carina Nebula, a massive gas and dust cloud located approximately 7500 light-years away from Earth. The two telescopes offer complementary views of the shadowy form, nicknamed the Cat’s Head Nebula, which reflects the 'magical'' process of star formation. Hubble’s visible-light view shows the cat as a dark, elongated dust pillar and hints of young forming stars, while Webb’s infrared-light imagery unveils many stars and other hidden details.

item.title: The universe in the eye of a telescope | Space photo of the day for Oct. 29, 2026
item.description: null The Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope reflects the stars at the La Silla Observatory in Chile. (Image credit: J. Rodrigues/ESO) Stars shine in the vast aluminum dish of the Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope (SEST) in this photograph captured by astronomer and astrophotographer José Rodrigues during a recent visit to the European Southern Observatory's La Silla Observatory in Chile. What is it? Rodrigues' image captures "airglow" infusing the night sky over La Silla with a soft orange glow, which is created as sunlight interacts with molecules in the upper atmosphere, according to the University of Lancaster . The subtle phenomenon can be seen reflected in the 15-meter (49-foot) primary dish of the SEST telescope along with the myriad stars of the Southern Hemisphere, as the dome of the ESO's 3.6-meter telescope looms in the background. Why is it incredible? "Despite knowing about its 15-meter diameter beforehand, I was amazed by its size," Rodrigues noted in the ESO image release. The SEST first opened its great eye to the universe in 1987, at which time it was the only large telescope in the Southern Hemisphere tasked with collecting submillimeter wavelengths of light that exist beyond the visible light spectrum. These specific wavelengths of light are emitted by wandering comets and colossal clouds of cold molecular dust and gas threaded throughout the Milky Way and beyond. SEST's observations improved our knowledge of ancient galaxies, star formation and so much more, with its perch 2,375 meters (7,792 feet) above sea level granting it a near unrivalled view of the heavens above. The SEST telescope was decommissioned in 2003, though its work was continued by the more capable Atacama Pathfinder Experiment (APEX) and the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA). With its working days over, the SEST telescope now stands as a quiet mirror reflecting the stars of the Southern Hemisphere night sky, seemingly pondering mysteries of the universe that it once tried to solve

item.title: Reps seek review of NCC phone rules over price hike fears
item.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for a review of the Nigerian Communications Commission’s (NCC) mobile device verification requirements over concerns that the policy could increase phone prices and lead to the wrongful blocking of legitimate used devices. The House warned that additional compliance costs under the framework could increase expenses for phone importers and retailers, with consumers, particularly low-income Nigerians, likely to bear the burden through higher prices. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by a Kano lawmaker, Sani Wakili, urging the commission to review the implementation of its device verification framework in consultation with relevant stakeholders. The framework, operated through the Device Management System and the Central Equipment Identity Register, enables the identification and verification of mobile phones and other SIM-enabled devices using their International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) numbers. Lawmakers noted that the enhanced verification requirements, which took effect on October 7, 2026, impose additional compliance obligations on newly imported devices, potentially raising operating costs for importers and retailers. They expressed concern that businesses could transfer the additional expenses to consumers, making mobile phones less affordable for Nigerians who rely on them for communication, education, banking and other commercial activities. The House also raised concerns about possible technical errors, database mismatches and limitations in the commission’s scanning and verification systems, warning that such challenges could result in legitimate devices being wrongly rejected or blocked. According to the lawmakers, the second-hand phone market could be particularly affected, given that used devices offer a more affordable alternative to new phones for many Nigerians. While acknowledging the NCC’s efforts to tackle counterfeit, cloned and stolen mobile phones, the House stressed that enforcement should not unfairly penalise legitimate businesses or restrict access to affordable communication devices. Consequently, the lawmakers urged the commission to review the framework’s implementation, simplify verification procedures and reduce compliance costs. They also called for a fair and accessible verification process for used and second-hand mobile phones to prevent legitimate devices from being wrongly flagged or blocked. To further examine the concerns, the House mandated its Committees on Communications and Commerce to engage the NCC and other relevant stakeholders on the implementation of the requirements and report back within four weeks for further legislative action. The Committee on Legislative Compliance was also directed to ensure compliance with the resolution. The proposed review comes amid growing reliance on mobile phones for essential economic and social activities, including digital financial services, online learning, electronic commerce an

item.title: Crypto Exchange HTX Agrees to Leave UK in Settlement With FCA
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Crypto Exchange HTX Agrees to Leave UK in Settlement With FCA Justin Sun’s HTX has agreed to leave the United Kingdom, closing the Financial Conduct Authority’s first enforcement case against a crypto firm over financial promotions. The regulator announced the settlement today, ending a High Court action that began in October 2025, according to Financial Times reporting . Under the court undertakings, Huobi Global S.A., the Panama-registered company behind the HTX brand, has promised not to communicate financial promotions that breach UK law across its website, apps and social media channels. The FCA says the exchange is no longer active in Britain. UK customers cannot deposit funds, and new users cannot register. Existing customers have 48 hours to withdraw assets before their accounts close. The regulator framed the outcome as a warning. Steve Smart, the FCA’s executive director of enforcement and market oversight, said that being based overseas does not place a firm beyond the reach of UK law. Smart said that ‘Crypto firms should be under no illusion: being based overseas does not put them beyond the reach of UK law. Our action means HTX is leaving the UK and can no longer target UK consumers. The message to other firms is clear: follow the rules or face the consequences.’ The regulator said HTX had failed to really engage over several rounds of talks of the case. Settlement talks began in March and were extended in June HTX settlement and background HTX presents a different account. The exchange says it has put measures in place to align with UK promotion rules. “We take local compliance requirements seriously and have proactively implemented measures to align with the UK’s financial promotion regulations,” the company said in a statement, according to Reuters. The settlement terms remain confidential, and the FCA says the deal involves no admission of liability or wrongdoing. Public reporting does not say whether any fine was paid. In May, the UK sanctioned Huobi Global over alleged support for Russia’s financial sector, listing HTX as another name for the designated entity. In July, the European Union named Huobi Global in its 21st Russia sanctions package and barred EU transactions with the exchange, stopping short of a full asset freeze. HTX says Huobi Global S.A. is distinct from the online exchange. Back in August, Kraken clients were briefly locked out of their accounts after receiving tiny amounts of cryptocurrency linked to sanctioned funds in what was known as a dust attack. Kraken said the attacks aimed to trigger compliance checks and spread sanctioned funds across platforms, causing operational disruptions for thousands of users. Around 12,000 transfers were reportedly sent from a wallet linked to HTX. Kraken’s compliance team quickly restored customer access while retaining the sanctioned funds and working with authorities to prevent further attacks. item.title: ‘I won’t waste my time talking about Amaechi’ — Oshiomhole
item.description: Senator Adams Oshiomhole has dismissed former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi as unreliable, saying he would not waste his time discussing the former minister. Oshiomhole spoke on TVC while reacting to Amaechi’s comments that President Bola Tinubu faces more challengers in the 2027 presidential election top challengers are from the South, while former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has fewer opponents because he is from the North. “If you know Amaechi, you won’t waste airtime talking about him,” Oshiomhole said. The former Edo State governor questioned Amaechi’s political consistency, citing his past dispute with Atiku over the African Democratic Congress presidential primary. According to Oshiomhole, Amaechi had accused Atiku of emerging from a fraudulent primary and challenged his victory in court. “Here is Amaechi on record in your TVC coverage and other network stations, who said that his own boss, the presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar, that the primary that produce him was a fraudulent process, and Atiku stole the mandate, he didn’t win the mandate. He didn’t stop there. Amaechi went to court to challenge Atiku that he stole the mandate,” he said. Oshiomhole added that Atiku later reached an agreement with Amaechi, claiming the former vice-president had asked him to share the mandate they allegedly obtained through a fraudulent process. “This is not social media, there are court documents, and Atiku went back to him and said okay, let’s share the stolen mandate together,” he said. Oshiomhole also referred to Amaechi’s political history, arguing that his rise to power and appointment as a minister were not the result of direct electoral victories. He said Amaechi became governor following a Supreme Court decision and was appointed minister by former President Muhammadu Buhari in 2015. “And I am not surprised that knowing what I know about him…he’s been very lucky that Supreme Court make him a governor without appearing on the ballot, and President Buhari made him a minister without voting for him in 2015, because I was a national player and later national chairman, so I know what I’m talking about,” Oshiomhole said. The senator further criticised Amaechi for describing other political figures as ethnic champions, arguing that the former governor had presented himself as the exception before the African Democratic Congress primaries. “He referred to Atiku as an ethnic champion. He referred to every other person as an ethnic champion. He was the only non-ethnic champion in the ADC before their primaries,” Oshiomhole said. He questioned Amaechi’s assessment of other political leaders, saying someone who dismisses others as ethnic champions should not be taken seriously when discussing leadership in a diverse country like Nigeria. The post ‘I won’t waste my time talking about Amaechi’ — Oshiomhole appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Understanding the Various Bitcoin Per Share Metrics
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Understanding the Various Bitcoin Per Share Metrics Bitcoin per share is one of the most important metrics for evaluating a Bitcoin treasury company. It measures how much bitcoin is attributable to each common share. However, there are several ways to calculate this figure, and each method provides different information about the economics of owning the common stock. Understanding these differences is essential for evaluating a company’s capital structure, measuring accretion, and determining the value attributable to common shareholders. Raw Bitcoin Per Share The simplest metric is raw Bitcoin Per Share (BPS). BPS = Total Bitcoin Holdings / Common Shares Outstanding This calculation divides the company’s bitcoin holdings by its existing common shares. It provides a straightforward measure of how much bitcoin is attributable to each currently outstanding share. The primary limitation is its treatment of potential dilution. A company may have warrants, convertible debt, or convertible preferred stock that could eventually become common shares. Raw BPS only counts existing shares, so it provides an incomplete picture of the potential future share count. Bitcoin Per Assumed Diluted Share Bitcoin Per Assumed Diluted Share (BPADS) addresses this limitation by incorporating the shares that would exist if all potentially dilutive securities converted into common stock. BPADS = Total Bitcoin Holdings / Assumed Diluted Shares Outstanding Because the assumed diluted share count is greater than or equal to the existing share count, BPADS is always less than or equal to raw BPS. This metric became widely cited beginning in 2024, particularly as Bitcoin treasury companies began using increasingly complex capital structures. BPADS provides a more conservative view of bitcoin ownership by incorporating potential dilution from outstanding securities. It becomes especially relevant for companies with substantial convertible debt, warrants, or convertible preferred stock. However, its assumption of full conversion can be overly conservative. Warrants and convertible debt may never convert if the common stock price remains below their conversion or exercise prices. Perpetual convertible preferred stock may also remain outstanding indefinitely if investors prefer receiving the preferred dividend rather than converting into common equity. Consequently, BPADS represents a fully diluted scenario rather than a forecast of the actual future share count. Net Bitcoin Per Share Both BPS and BPADS share another major limitation: they measure gross bitcoin holdings without accounting for senior claims on the company’s assets. Common equity sits at the bottom of the capital structure. Debt holders and preferred shareholders generally have priority over common shareholders according to their contractual rights. These senior claims matter because they reduce the assets ultimately attributable to common equity. Net Bitcoin Per Share (Net BPS) addresses this by de

item.title: Imo West: South-East Youths congratulate Okorocha, urge Uzodimma to respect the ruling
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu The South-East Youths Stakeholders Forum has congratulated former Imo State Governor, Senator Rochas Okorocha, following a Federal High Court judgment declaring him the winner of the All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial primary for Imo West ahead of the 2027 general elections. The forum also urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to comply with the court’s directives and take the necessary steps to recognise Okorocha as the party’s candidate for the district. The judgment, delivered on Thursday by Justice Obiora Egwuatu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, ordered Governor Hope Uzodimma of Imo State to stop presenting himself as the APC candidate for the Imo West senatorial election scheduled for January 16, 2027. The court held that evidence before it established that Okorocha secured the majority of votes cast during the APC senatorial primary conducted on May 18, 2026, which was monitored by INEC. It consequently directed the APC to submit Okorocha’s name to the electoral commission as its candidate for the election. The ruling followed a legal challenge by Okorocha against Uzodimma’s recognition as the party’s candidate. INEC’s previously reported official results had listed Uzodimma as the winner of the primary, a position Okorocha contested in court. Reacting to the judgment, the forum described the development as significant and expressed confidence that the rule of law would prevail in resolving political disputes. In a statement made available to journalists, the chairman of the forum’s Imo State chapter, Comrade Ifeanyi Nwosu, said respect for judicial decisions remained fundamental to democracy, justice, peace and political stability. The forum called on INEC to take the necessary steps to implement the judgment in accordance with the court’s directives and applicable laws. It also appealed to Uzodimma and his supporters to respect the ruling, embrace reconciliation and work towards a united APC ahead of the 2027 general elections. According to the group, unity, mutual understanding and collective commitment among party leaders and stakeholders are essential to strengthening the APC and advancing its electoral objectives. The forum further reaffirmed its commitment to mobilising youths across the South-East in support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and APC candidates in future elections. It urged party leaders and stakeholders in Imo State to set aside their differences and work together in the interest of the party. item.title: 2027: INEC fears poll disruption in insecure areas
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has raised concerns that insecurity could disrupt or prevent the conduct of the 2027 general elections in some parts of the country. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, expressed the concern on Tuesday in Gombe while addressing participants at the North-East Zonal Interactive Staff Meeting and Operational Readiness Assessment for the 2027 general elections. Amupitan described insecurity in some parts of the country as a major challenge to the conduct of credible elections, calling for urgent and coordinated action by security agencies to protect the electoral process. He said he would engage the National Security Adviser, the Chief of Army Staff and other senior security officials upon his return to Abuja to discuss measures to address the threats and create a safer environment for the elections. The INEC chairman said the commission would adopt a proactive approach to electoral security rather than wait for threats to escalate before responding. He added that INEC was strengthening collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, the Department of State Services, the Armed Forces and other relevant agencies through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES). According to him, the collaboration is designed to improve intelligence-sharing, security coordination and operational preparedness ahead of the 2027 polls. The concerns come as INEC intensifies preparations for the elections, with insecurity posing potential risks to the movement of electoral personnel, distribution of sensitive election materials and participation of voters in affected communities. Amupitan stressed that sustained cooperation between electoral authorities and security agencies would be critical to ensuring that Nigerians could exercise their democratic rights without fear or intimidation. He said early intervention, effective deployment of security personnel and a coordinated response to security threats were necessary to prevent insecurity from undermining the credibility, inclusiveness and peaceful conduct of the 2027 general elections. The post 2027: INEC fears poll disruption in insecure areas appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Contractor to Civil Servant: NASA Welcomes Jared Spiers
item.description: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) Jared Spiers, electrical engineering technician at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, poses for a photograph with the Thad Cochran Test Stand in the background on Oct. 28, 2026. Spiers is now a NASA civil servant at Stennis as part of the administrator’s directive to strengthen technical core competencies within the civil service workforce. NASA/Danny Nowlin Jared Spiers had an interest in contributing to NASA’s mission long before becoming a civil servant for the agency. Growing up close to NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, and hearing about his father’s work there, he gained a firsthand connection to the nation’s space program. Before graduating high school, he knew exactly where he wanted to work. Spiers graduated from Pearl River Community College in 2017, where he earned three associate degrees in instrumentation, electronics, and electrical technology. He started working at NASA Stennis as a contractor on the Monday following graduation. Spiers contributed to the mission of returning to the Moon through his work at the Thad Cochran Test Stand (B-1/B-2), a facility originally constructed to test Saturn V rocket stages during the Apollo Program. He helped prepare the stand for the Green Run test series of the first core stage for NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket before the successful Artemis I test flight. “Being hands-on with the rocket was a whole different experience,” said Spiers. “Childhood me would have been crazily excited to see it.” This work helped lay the foundation for the Artemis II test flight around the Moon last April. During that mission, the first astronauts to fly aboard NASA’s Orion spacecraft traveled farther in space than humans ever have before. This past summer, in June 2026, Spiers transitioned to a civil servant role under NASA’s workforce directive to restore core competencies. “When I joined NASA, it meant a lot more. It felt like a goal achieved,” said Spiers. “As a contractor, I was never treated any differently, but now with NASA, you feel even more a part of the team. There is more ownership and a very significant sense of pride.” The ownership Spiers takes on as an electrical engineering technician is evident during his 12-hour shifts that begin at 6 a.m. He is part of the team preparing the stand for stage testing of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket. This commercial partnership directly supports NASA’s work to achieve the goal of landing American astronauts on the Moon and building a Moon Base. Spiers’ technical acumen is put to work daily as he ensures facility electronics are operational so accurate data can be collected. He runs conduit and cabling, connects data-collecting instruments, and ensures motor valves operate as intended. The work is fast paced, but Spiers takes pride in making sure everything is done right. For Spiers, NASA is truly a family affair. His father
